about: The cars. Speeds are game metres per second (top speed times 3.6 is the km/h on the dial), acceleration is m/s2 from a standstill, grip is the sideways g a car holds before it slides, brake is m/s2. These are arcade numbers in the right order, not test figures: a GT3 RS is quicker than a GTI everywhere, and a Volvo 240 is a Volvo 240. pace is how much of its grip an AI driver uses through a corner; style picks the body shape, kit race gives a widebody racer its flares, splitter, vents, swan-neck wing, cage and door number, and kit bronco an open, lifted Bronco with a roll cage, a surfboard and a family aboard.

stats.accel: acceleration from rest, m/s2; it fades toward top speed
stats.drift: how hard the car rotates in a drift, 1 is normal
stats.mass: tonnes, for who wins a bump
stats.drs: the GT3 RS's drag reduction: open on a straight, top speed rises by vmax and drag falls by drag (shares); it shuts on the brakes or in a corner
stats.engine: for the sound and the dials only: cylinders, idle and redline rpm, where it changes up flat out (shift, if not near the redline), the strength of each partial of the engine cycle (partials, the first being rpm / 120 Hz; the GT3 RS's are measured from an onboard recording, 653 frames above 5,500 rpm), the gearbox (pdk and dsg are twin-clutch, manual, auto) and the speed in km/h at the redline in each gear

player.name: VW Golf GTI
player.note: Mk7. The car half the queue came in. Balanced, easy, quick enough.

player.name: Porsche 911 GT3 RS
player.note: 992. Fastest car in the lot, and it knows it. Grip for days, a little nervous on the jumps, and DRS: press X on a straight.

player.name: Ford Bronco Sasquatch
player.note: 2025, two doors, top and doors off, the whole family aboard and a surfboard on the cage. Drives, sounds and shifts exactly like the GT3 RS, DRS and all. Reggae on.

player.name: Honda Civic Type R
player.note: FL5. Front-wheel drive lap record hunter. Brakes late, turns in hard.

player.name: Mazda MX-5
player.note: NA, pop-up lights. Slow on the straights, a joy everywhere else. Drifts on a thought.

player.name: Volvo 240 Estate
player.note: 1989, 300,000 km, a roof box. Slow, soft and heavy. Nothing it hits is safe.

queueGap.desc: Space between cars waiting in the queue, game metres.

release.desc: Seconds between one car's barrier going up and the next car's.

trafficCount.desc: Slow cars already out on the lap when you go through the gate.

slip.desc: Slipstream: within dist metres behind a car and lat metres of its line, after build seconds you get gain more top speed.

boost.desc: Drift mini-turbo: hold a drift t1 seconds for the blue spark (b1 seconds of boost), t2 for orange (b2 seconds). gain is the extra push and top speed while it lasts.

grass.desc: On the grass: extra slowing per second and the share of top speed you can hold.

wall.desc: Speed kept after hitting the Armco square on is less; glancing off it costs little.

rubber.desc: The kart-game rubber band: a rival more than ahead metres up the road drives at slow of its pace, one more than behind metres back at fast, so the race stays close.

modes.desc: The driving modes, for the player only. wall is the speed kept hitting the Armco square on, grass the grass for that mode. brake is the share of grip the brake aid lets you carry into a corner before it brakes for you: under 1 it keeps you inside the grip, over 1 it steps in only when you are well over it, 0 is off. guard steers you off the Armco: it looks look seconds ahead and starts within margin metres of the wall, gain is how firmly, brake how hard it brakes when the turn back needs more grip than there is. Expert is the race's own grass and Armco with no aids.

etiquette.desc: Ring etiquette: a car with a quicker one closing from behind (within behind metres, closing faster than closing m/s; a racer only for a car racer m/s quicker) puts its right blinker on, moves over to keep of the half-road on the right and lifts to lift of its speed, until the other is done metres past. Only where the road for the next clear metres has no bend tighter than radius metres: nobody moves over in a tight corner. Drivers differ: each has a reaction time and a courtesy, and one below ignore never moves over.

gravity.desc: Game gravity, m/s2. A bit above real so the cars land from the jumps before the next corner.
